description: A problem the compiler reports with a code such as CS0103 and a file position, which stops the program from being built at all.
An object that describes a problem found while the program runs, such as `IndexOutOfRangeException`, and that ends the program unless some code catches it.
The list of method calls that were running when an exception happened, read from the top, where the first line naming your code is usually the place to look.
The statement that creates an exception and stops the current method at once, as in `throw new ArgumentException("...", nameof(text));`.
A `try` block runs code, the first matching `catch` block handles an exception of its type, and the `finally` block runs in every case.
A check at the top of a method that returns or throws early on bad input, so the rest of the method can trust its input.
A small method that calls your code with chosen input and checks the result, written in three parts: arrange, act and assert.
